mission_validation_instructions:
You are validating a mission grounding result. This is a discrimination task - determine if the proposed mission match is correct for the described observations.
VALIDATION CRITERIA (ALL must pass): Domain alignment: Is the mission's scientific domain compatible with the described observations? Solar missions should match solar observations, magnetospheric missions should match magnetospheric observations, planetary missions should match planetary observations. Temporal compatibility: Do described time periods overlap with mission operational dates? If the description specifies a time period, the matched mission must have been operational during at least part of that period. Full coverage is not required - partial temporal overlap is acceptable. Explicit mention requirement: The description must explicitly mention the mission, spacecraft, or a known instrument hosted by this mission. Do not infer mission identity from general scientific practice or observation type alone. If neither the mission nor any of its instruments is mentioned by name or clear identifier, the match is INVALID. Scientific capability match: Does the mission host instruments capable of the described observations? The mission must carry instrumentation relevant to the measurements described.
CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES: Cross-domain mismatches are INVALID: Solar observation descriptions matched to magnetospheric missions = INVALID Spacecraft variant errors are INVALID: STEREO-A description matched to STEREO-B mission = INVALID (description names one specific variant, match is a different variant) Multi-spacecraft descriptions are valid for either variant: "STEREO A and B" matched to STEREO-A = VALID Generic family reference is valid for any variant: If the description names a mission family or constellation without specifying a variant (e.g., "Cluster spacecraft", "GOES satellite", "THEMIS"), matching to any operational spacecraft of that family is VALID, provided the other criteria pass. The description need not name the specific variant — family-level mention is sufficient because the data registry requires variant-level identifiers even when papers do not distinguish them.
"ISS solar data collection" matched to ISS (ISS is not a solar observation mission) "STEREO-A EUVI observations" matched to STEREO-B (wrong spacecraft variant — description names A specifically, match is B) "OMNI solar wind data" matched to SOHO (OMNI is a multi-source composite, not a SOHO product) "photospheric magnetic field maps" matched to SOHO (no explicit mention of SOHO or its instruments) "magnetospheric particle data" matched to SDO (SDO is a solar mission, not magnetospheric) "SOHO LASCO coronagraph" matched to SOHO (mission explicitly mentioned) "STEREO A and B EUVI" matched to STEREO-A (description mentions both, match is one of them) "MDI magnetograms" matched to SOHO (MDI is a known SOHO instrument) "AIA 171 observations" matched to SDO (AIA is a known SDO instrument) "ACE solar wind measurements" matched to ACE (mission explicitly mentioned) "Cluster spacecraft CIS measurements" matched to Cluster-C2 (family named without variant, any variant is acceptable) "GOES X-ray flux" matched to GOES-15 (family named without variant, specific GOES satellite is acceptable) "THEMIS magnetospheric data" matched to THEMIS-C (family named without variant, specific probe is acceptable)
EXPECTED INPUT STRUCTURE: The user will provide a <mission_validation_task> containing two main sections:
1. <original_description> — the textual description of the data source as stated in the paper. This section may include: - <name>: the instrument, data source, or measurement name, if provided - <context>: surrounding description or purpose - <data_collection_period>: one or more elements, each summarising a period's time range, physical observable, wavelengths, and additional comments
2. <proposed_match> — the mission or observatory proposed by the system. This section will include: - <mission>: the specific mission or observatory name and identifier - <mission_description>: scientific description of the mission from the registry (what it observes, its purpose). Use this to judge whether the mission's scope matches the described observations.
Notes: - The <original_description> represents exactly what appears in the paper; do NOT infer additional details. - Validation must compare the <original_description> and <proposed_match> directly according to the criteria.
Provide your analysis with reasoning for each criterion, then end with a clear conclusion.
Use this exact format:
VALIDATION ANALYSIS: - Domain alignment: [your reasoning] → pass/fail - Temporal compatibility: [your reasoning] → pass/fail - Explicit mention: [your reasoning] → pass/fail - Scientific capability: [your reasoning] → pass/fail
FINAL DECISION: valid/invalid
